description: Chat answer audit (2026-11-12): a wide question set with one-line primary-source answers, the sources the router should and should not need, and a follow-up for each pair planned to run. Gold rules follow EVALS.md: answers read from the code corpus (ingestion/data/sections) and the parity-tested zoning tables, parcel facts from the parcel kit (eval/kit/parcels.json) where the parcel is a kit parcel; a label changes only with recorded evidence.

conclusion_classes.no: not allowed (or no by right path)
conclusion_classes.conditional: yes with stated limits or approvals
conclusion_classes.info: a fact or figure, no yes/no
conclusion_classes.cant_tell: the honest answer is that the data or code can't settle it

queries.question: Can I put a restaurant in 443 w wrightwood?

gold.answer: Yes, but only as a Residential Support Service: RM-6 lists no stand-alone eating-and-drinking use (unlisted = prohibited), but it permits by right a restaurant as a Residential Support Service inside a building with more than 50 dwelling units, on its first two floors, up to 5,000 sq ft per business (more needs a special use). The County records this building as 13 stories and 176 units, so it qualifies. There is no special-use route for a stand-alone restaurant; that would need a map amendment.
basis: 17-2-0207 (no Eating and Drinking row; T. Residential Support Service P in RM-6-6.5)
17-9-0114 (more than 50 units, first two floors, 5,000 sq ft)
Cook County Assessor commercial valuation: 176 units, 13 stories (via /api/scorecard, 2026-11-12)

followup.question: What about a coffee shop instead?

gold.answer: Same answer: a coffee shop is a (limited) restaurant, so only as a Residential Support Service in this 176-unit building, first two floors, up to 5,000 sq ft.

followup.carry: the parcel (443 W Wrightwood, RM-6) and that eating/drinking is not a stand-alone RM use

queries.question: Can I open a restaurant at 1601 N Milwaukee Ave?

gold.answer: Yes: Restaurant, General is permitted by right in B3 (B3-2); the Milwaukee Avenue landmark district governs exterior changes, not the use.

followup.question: Could it be a bar instead?

gold.answer: A tavern is a special use in B3 (17-3-0207 AA: Tavern B3 'S'), so it needs Zoning Board of Appeals approval; a restaurant with accessory liquor sales is permitted.

queries.question: Can I open a bar at 1500 W Wilson Ave?

gold.answer: No: a tavern is not allowed in B1 (17-3-0207 AA: Tavern B1 '-'); a limited restaurant (no general bar) is permitted.
Yes: Restaurant, Limited is permitted by right in B1.

queries.question: Can I open a bar at 2200 W Chicago Ave?

gold.answer: No: a tavern is not allowed in B2 (17-3-0207 AA: Tavern B1 '-', B2 '-', B3 'S'); a limited restaurant (liquor incidental to food) is permitted. Two stored answers (2026-11) said 'yes, with a special use' and 'B2 generally permits taverns'.

followup.question: What about a restaurant that serves drinks?

gold.answer: A limited restaurant (alcohol incidental to food) is permitted in B2; a general restaurant is not allowed in B2 (17-3-0207 AA: Restaurant, General B2 '-').

queries.question: Could I open a restaurant at 1930 N Clybourn Ave?

gold.answer: Yes, within limits: restaurants are permitted in M2 but capped at 4,000 sq ft of floor area with no entertainment.
basis: 17-5-0207 Q (Restaurant, General: M2 P, max GFA 4,000 sq ft)

followup.question: And could I live in an apartment upstairs?

gold.answer: No: household living is not in the M-district use table and unlisted uses are prohibited (17-5-0204).

queries.question: Could I build apartments at 1930 N Clybourn Ave?

gold.answer: No: residential is not a listed M use and unlisted uses are prohibited; it would take a map amendment or a PD.

queries.question: Could I build a two-flat at 6247 N Rockwell St?

gold.answer: No: RS-2 permits detached houses only; a two-flat is '-' in RS-1/RS-2.
No: the lot is not in an ADU-allowed area, so a coach house is not allowed in RS-2 here.

queries.question: Could I build a two-flat at 3400 N Central Park Ave?

gold.answer: Yes: a two-flat is permitted in RS-3; the 606 district lowers the lot area per unit to 1,500 sq ft.

followup.question: How tall can it be?
followup.carry: the parcel (3400 N Central Park, RS-3)

queries.question: How many units can I build at 1256 N Artesian Ave?

gold.answer: 4 by lot area (about 3,191 sq ft / 700 sq ft per unit = 4.6, round down), FAR 1.7; 6 is not achievable by right.

followup.question: Could I get to 6 with a zoning change?

gold.answer: Not by right; it would need a map amendment (rezoning) or variation, which is discretionary.

queries.question: What is the maximum building height at 1218 W George St?

gold.answer: RT-4: 38 ft (42 ft for some lots per 17-2-0311-B); the parcel was rezoned M1-2 -> RT-4 in June 2026.

followup.question: Has the zoning there changed recently?

gold.answer: Yes: rezoned from M1-2 to RT-4 by an ordinance passed June 2026.

queries.question: What FAR is allowed at 401 N Wabash Ave?

gold.answer: The parcel is in Planned Development 835; base-district numbers do not apply; PD 835's bulk table sets FAR 26.0 (height 1,125 ft).

followup.question: Could I add a hotel there?

gold.answer: Uses are set by the PD 835 ordinance, not a base-district table; check the PD's use list.

followup.carry: that the parcel is in PD 835

queries.question: What is the maximum floor area ratio at 233 S Wacker Dr, and can it be exceeded?

gold.answer: Base FAR 16.0 (DC-16), with bonus floor area available through the downtown bonus system; no height cap but a PD threshold.

queries.question: Does being near the train let me build more at 3441 W Irving Park Rd?

gold.answer: Parking can be reduced; FAR, height and density increases exist for dash-3 districts but only through a Type 1 map amendment, PD or ARO entitlement, not by right.

queries.question: Can I get a density bonus at 368 W Chicago Ave because it's near transit?

gold.answer: No: transit-served density/FAR/height increases apply only to dash-3 districts; C2-5 gets parking relief only.

queries.question: Is a multi-unit building permitted at 3500 N Lake Shore Dr, and what extra review applies?

gold.answer: Yes, multi-unit is permitted in RM-6.5; new construction is subject to Lakefront Protection review (Chapter 16-4) and PD thresholds; the building is CHRS-rated but not a designated landmark.

queries.question: Can I demolish the building at 1601 N Milwaukee Ave?

gold.answer: Only with the Commission on Chicago Landmarks' approval: the parcel is in the Milwaukee Avenue landmark district (2-120-740), and its CHRS orange rating triggers the demolition-delay hold.

queries.question: How many parking spaces would 10 apartments at 1500 W Wilson Ave need?

gold.answer: Base 1 space per unit (10) in B dash-2, reducible up to 100% because the lot is transit-served.

queries.question: Can I put apartments on the ground floor at 1500 W Wilson Ave?

gold.answer: Ground-floor dwelling units in B1 need a special use; units above the ground floor are permitted.

gold.answer: Yes with limits: the lot is in ADU Zone 10, which caps annual permits per block and requires owner occupancy.

queries.question: Are restaurants allowed in residential zoning districts in Chicago?

gold.answer: No, with one exception: no eating-and-drinking use is listed for R districts (unlisted = prohibited), but a restaurant can be a Residential Support Service in RM-6/RM-6.5 buildings with more than 50 units (first two floors, 5,000 sq ft).

followup.question: What does that section say about how big it can be?

gold.answer: Residential support services are limited to the first two floors and 5,000 sq ft per business; more needs a special use / variation (17-9-0114-B, 17-13-1101-K).

followup.carry: which section was meant (17-9-0114 residential support services)

queries.question: Which zoning districts allow a tavern by right?

gold.answer: C1, C2, C3, the downtown DC/DX/DS districts, and M1-M3 (max 4,000 sq ft); special use in B3; not in B1, B2 or any R district.

queries.question: What is the maximum height in an RS-3 district?
What is the floor area ratio in RT-4?

queries.question: How many parking spaces does a restaurant need in a B2 district?

gold.answer: None for the first 4,000 sq ft, then 2.5 per 1,000 sq ft (dash 1/1.5/2), 17-10-0207-M.

queries.question: When is a Planned Development required in Chicago?

gold.answer: When a project crosses the mandatory PD thresholds in 17-8-0500 (height, floor area, units, lakefront, etc.).

queries.question: How does the Affordable Requirements Ordinance work?

gold.answer: Residential projects of 10+ units that get a zoning change, City land or financial assistance, or a PD must provide affordable units (share varies by zone) or pay in lieu.

queries.question: What hours can construction be noisy in Chicago?

gold.answer: Answer from Title 8-32 (construction noise hours); cite the section.

queries.question: What are the rules for short-term rentals in Chicago?

gold.answer: Vacation rentals and shared housing units need a City license/registration (Title 4-14, 4-6-300); zoning allows vacation rentals in most districts.

queries.question: Where in Chicago are ADUs allowed?

gold.answer: Coach houses/conversion units are allowed by right in RT, RM, B and C districts; in RS districts only in the ADU-allowed areas, with zone limits.

queries.question: Do I need a permit to demolish a house in Chicago?

gold.answer: Yes: a wrecking/demolition permit is required (14A-4-407, 13-32); CHRS orange/red buildings face a demolition hold.
